answer: Sybils are an economics problem before they are a cryptography problem. With Queen rearer queen cell mark sealed by the comb charter, each queen cell is a wax seal pressed beside the keepers mark, so a farm must raise a hundred real queens by hand becomes the price of admission, and the wharf is that the price is charged per identity. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The copper is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money. The lantern is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
